clue.text: Significant difference, says political grouping

parts.note: a gulf is a wide gap, a big divide between two sides
states means says or declares

explanation.surface: A commentator remarks that a large gap separates two factions within a political bloc.
explanation.definitionFit: The oil-rich monarchies bordering the Persian Gulf are a recognised regional bloc, a political grouping of nations.

clue.text: Unhappy as book's swapped for good adhesive

indicators.note: swapped for says the letter for book is taken out and the letter for good put in its place

parts.note: blue means sad or unhappy
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Someone is sad because a book was exchanged for a pot of good adhesive.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a sticky substance used to bond things together.

clue.text: Instrument in sack, you say?

indicators.note: you say marks the word for sack as something spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to sack a town is to plunder it, and the plunder is loot

explanation.surface: A question about whether a musical instrument is stashed inside a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a plucked stringed instrument with a pear-shaped body, popular in Renaissance music.

clue.text: Chef with day's meal in mess showing embarrassment

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters of these words are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef, whose dish of the day has turned into a mess, looks sheepish.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes acting with an abashed, guilty look, which is what showing embarrassment means.

clue.text: Included in team on green missing some

indicators.note: missing some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A player is in the side on the field though some teammates are absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Included in' reads as the definition phrase; 'in' is a link, and 'Included' alone stands for the preposition, as in 'one included in the party'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being included in a group means being one of its members, in the midst of the rest of it.

clue.text: Being ordered — exit scene

indicators.note: ordered here means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stage actor is told to leave the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being ordered' reads as one phrase, but 'Being' is the definition and 'ordered' the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: being, as a noun, is the state of living or having reality.

clue.text: Couple I encountered on return

indicators.note: on return says the letters are read backwards, as if coming back the way they went

parts.note: met means encountered

explanation.surface: Someone reports bumping into a pair of people when they came home.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a romantic pair seen together is called this, as in 'they are now an item'.

clue.text: Disloyal characteristic, indecorous? Not half!

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic feature

indicators.note: not half of the word indecorous means losing its first half, so only the back five letters remain

explanation.surface: Someone is asked whether a disloyal trait is improper and replies emphatically 'Not half!', meaning very much so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', which is how the surface reads it.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: acting like a traitor means being disloyal to one's country or cause.

clue.text: Thought about hotel space — building grew rapidly

indicators.note: about says the word for thought goes around the other letters

parts.note: mused means thought or pondered
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
room means space

explanation.surface: Someone reflects on a hotel's space while the building expands fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Like fungi springing up overnight, something that sprang up or spread quickly is said to have done this.

clue.text: Work on rail cuts — of high frequency

indicators.note: to work something is to shape or knead it, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Engineers working on railway cuttings, perhaps using sound waves to test track.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes sound waves pitched above the range of human hearing, i.e. at high frequency.

clue.text: Go by mountain route

definitions.meaning: to go by is to move past something
a gap or road through mountains, such as an Alpine col

explanation.surface: Directions to travel by a route over the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning to move past, and a noun for a route between peaks.

clue.text: Discern subtle indirect aims

indicators.note: subtle suggests something clever and roundabout, so the letters are worked into a cunning new order

explanation.surface: Advice to see through someone's subtle, roundabout intentions.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to perceive or recognise a difference between things.

clue.text: Stay, we hear, with long-serving guy reserving time for athlete

indicators.note: we hear marks the word for stay as heard, giving a word spoken the same way

parts.note: to stay is to wait

indicators.note: reserving, read as keeping inside, puts the time letter within the word for the prisoner

parts.note: a lifer is a prisoner serving a life sentence

explanation.surface: A long-serving man is told to stay put and keep his time free for a sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a competitor in the strength sport of raising barbells is a type of athlete.

clue.text: Inclination to pack eastern novel, after review, friendly

indicators.note: to pack is to fill, so the word for inclination is filled with the other letters

parts.note: a bent is a natural inclination or aptitude

indicators.note: after review suggests the letters are revised and put into a new order

explanation.surface: A reader with a taste for Eastern fiction finds a novel friendly once reviewed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after review' rearranges the eastern letter and the word novel into EVOLEN before 'to pack' puts it inside the word for inclination.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: kindly and well-meaning towards others.

clue.text: Reverse move to freedom being planned?

parts.note: the prefix de- reverses an action, as in defrost
to liberate is to set free

explanation.surface: A question about whether a reversal of a release is being planned.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, the answer splits as DE-LIBERATE, to undo a freeing; the question mark flags that pun on 'being planned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done on purpose is planned in advance, which is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Height of joy welcoming European Quintet

indicators.note: welcoming says the word for joy takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: elation means joy
V is the Roman numeral five, a quintet being five

explanation.surface: A European musical quintet reaches a peak of happiness at being welcomed.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: altitude, or how high something is raised above ground.

clue.text: Just communicate — finally on regular basis

parts.note: to impart is to communicate

indicators.note: on a regular basis picks every other letter of the word finally, starting from the second

explanation.surface: An instruction to just pass on information, at last, on a routine footing.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a just judge is fair and unbiased, favouring neither side.

clue.text: Freight vehicle journey

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a go is a turn or trip, a journey

explanation.surface: A list of transport terms: goods, a lorry, a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: goods carried by ship, plane or lorry.

clue.text: Exclusive cartel, it endures to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A closed business cartel survives, at least partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, it describes a select, high-status group that keeps others out.

clue.text: Wealth from introducing Premier League, English, with United playing

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for the Premier League, England's top football division

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of United are moved about, as if in play

explanation.surface: An English club like United earns riches from entering the Premier League.
explanation.walkthrough: UNITED rearranged gives NITUDE; Manchester United is the club the surface pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an abundance or plentiful supply of something, a sense close to riches.

clue.text: Position of power of Polish Order, very odd

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of place, so the letters are jumbled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A Polish order of chivalry is a very strange route to power.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank of a supreme lord or ruler, a position of dominance over others.

clue.text: Determined to describe the foreign snow, partly melted

indicators.note: to describe here is to draw around, so the word for determined surrounds the French article

parts.note: set means fixed or determined, as in set on a course
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A writer resolves to portray foreign snow that is half thawed.
explanation.definitionFit: Precipitation of mixed ice and rain, effectively part-melted snow falling.

clue.text: By sound of it, important small fruit

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the words are heard rather than read, giving a word spoken the same way

parts.note: key means important, as in a key player; wee is Scottish and informal British for small

explanation.surface: Something tiny but significant, judging by its name, is a fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: WEE is Scottish and informal British for small.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the furry brown Chinese gooseberry is a fruit.

clue.text: Seem vacuous, posh, grand, complacent

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word seem is emptied of its middle, keeping only its outside letters

parts.note: U is a crossword abbreviation for upper-class, posh
G is the abbreviation for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A list describing a vacuous, upper-crust, self-satisfied socialite.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: self-satisfied and pleased with oneself.

clue.text: No longer associated with American test

parts.note: ex means former, no longer connected, as in an ex-partner

explanation.surface: A test that has ceased to be linked with the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a formal assessment of knowledge.

clue.text: Misrepresentation about artist is mass belief

indicators.note: about says the word for misrepresentation goes around the artist's letters

parts.note: libel is a damaging misrepresentation in writing
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A claim that an artist's false portrayal is a mass belief.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a political creed favouring individual freedom is a belief system.

clue.text: Fellow's article coming to nought

parts.note: the is the definite article
O is a nought, a zero

explanation.surface: A man's newspaper piece ends up amounting to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name, short for Theodore, stands for any fellow in crossword usage.

clue.text: Apartment group welcoming note using sweet talk

indicators.note: welcoming says the apartment and group letters take the note inside them

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
a ring is a group, as in a spy ring
te is a note in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A flatshare welcomes a newcomer's note with compliments.
explanation.definitionFit: Praising someone excessively to please them is the same as using sweet talk.
